summary: Estimating a microphone's coloration from 10 s of speech with a population prior made the residual coloration worse, so automatic microphone correction from speech stays out of the product.
method: Empirical Bayes per 1/3-octave band (100 Hz-8 kHz): estimate = w (measured - population mean), w = s_c^2 / (s_c^2 + s_speaker^2). Prior from fit-split users without coloration, s_c from calibrate-split users with coloration, tested on test-split users. Colorations: low shelf, high shelf and two bells, each within +-6 dB, applied to the noisy reverberant capture.
predefined_rule: lower residual coloration RMS than no correction, speaker-clustered 95% CI of the reduction above 0, and at most 5% of users more than 1 dB RMS worse

corpus.speech: VoiceBank clean sets (VCTK subset), CC BY 4.0, 48 kHz, 88 speakers
corpus.noise: DEMAND channel 1, CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record 1227121), 18 environments
corpus.rooms: synthetic 48 kHz stochastic room responses (RT60 0.2-0.7 s)
corpus.splits: speakers, noise environments and room seeds disjoint: fit / calibrate / test

limitations: Speaker, room and noise spread (2-9 dB per band) is as large as the simulated colorations.
Per-model microphone profiles remain a separate possibility, limited by distance and placement.
